The Off-Season Problem

Why Most Off-Season Programmes Fail Ultimate Players

Most training programs available to Ultimate players fall into one of two extremes. Neither of them prepares your body for the physical demands of high-level tournament play.

✕
The Unqualified Player

Passion Without Clinical Science

Created by athletes who know the sport, but have no formal medical, physiotherapy, or sports science qualifications. They prescribe generic gym splits, copy-paste workouts, and lack the knowledge of tissue load capacity, tendon adaptation, and injury mechanics.

Result: Hamstring strains & overuse flare-ups by Tournament 1.
✕
The Generic Qualified Coach

Theory Without Ultimate Context

Created by coaches who hold general fitness qualifications, but have zero real-world experience working with Ultimate Frisbee athletes. They don't understand the violent rotational torque of low-release pivots, asymmetrical turf cuts, or the brutal endurance required for Sunday finals.

Result: Gym strength that doesn't transfer to game speed on turf.
✓
The Hybrid Standard

Clinical Rehab Meets Game Speed

Justin Lim represents the rare combination of both: a Chartered Physiotherapist (MSc Advanced Physiotherapy) & S&C Coach who treats high-level athletes including Premier League footballers, alongside GB squad and World Ultimate Championship (WUC) players in London.

Result: Resilient joints, bulletproof hamstrings, and championship speed.

3. Rapid Capacity & Strength Self-Screen

Test A: Single-Leg Hamstring Bridge (Knee at 60°)

Lie on back, heel dug into ground with knee slightly bent (not 90°), lift hips on one leg.

Test B: Copenhagen Side Plank (Adductor Capacity)

Side plank with top leg resting on a bench or chair, bottom leg hanging free.

Test C: Ankle Knee-to-Wall Dorsiflexion

Toes facing wall, lunge knee forward to touch wall without lifting heel.

Periodisation Architecture
Weeks 1 – 4 • Phase 1
Joints & Tissue Capacity

Rebuild tendon resilience, eccentric hamstring loading (RDLs, sliders), Copenhagen adductor progressions, and soleus endurance.

Weeks 5 – 8 • Phase 2
Max Force & Torque

Volume: 2 Gym + 1 Power Session

Deceleration & Game Speed

Translating gym strength onto grass and turf, allowing the body to confidently absorb and generate force to the ground.

Volume: 2 Gym + 2 Field Sessions

The 12-Week Season Programme

And you need to systematically progress your physicality as an Ultimate player so you can reach the next level.

Tendon and Joint Capacity
Weeks 1 – 4 • Phase 1

Joints and Tissue Capacity

Before lifting heavy or sprinting max velocity, the programme rebuilds resilience in tendons and ensures there is adequate joint mobility.

  • ✓ Long-length eccentric hamstring loading (RDLs, Sliders)
  • ✓ Copenhagen adductor progressions
  • ✓ Lumbar rotational stability & pelvic control
  • ✓ Soleus endurance & bent-knee calf capacity
  • ✓ Thoracic mobility & rotator cuff deceleration
Volume: 2 gym and 1 mobility session Load Capacity
Rotational Power
Weeks 5 – 8 • Phase 2

Max Force & Rotational Torque

Phase 2 builds true horsepower. Target maximum bilateral force, single-leg stability, and the hip-to-shoulder kinetic chain for effortless 60m sprints.

  • ✓ Low-handle trap bar deadlifts (Explosive concentric)
  • ✓ Rear-foot elevated split squats & lateral lunges
  • ✓ Med-ball rotational shotput & whip drills
  • ✓ Landmine multi-planar rotational press
Volume: 2 gym and 1 power session Peak Force
Deceleration & COD
Weeks 9 – 12 • Phase 3

Deceleration & Tournament Speed

Translating gym strength onto grass and turf, allowing the body to confidently absorb and generate force to the ground.

  • ✓ Penultimate step braking & 5-10-5 agility drill
  • ✓ Flying 10m & curved top-speed sprint mechanics
  • ✓ Cleats-on drop jumps into reactive redirection
  • ✓ Repeat Sprint Ability (RSA) D-line intervals
Volume: 2 Gym + 2 Field Sessions Game-Speed

Chartered Physiotherapist & Strength & Conditioning Coach

Justin bridges the gap between clinical rehab and high-performance sport. He specialises in lower limb injuries, having helped hundreds of patients recovering from ACL reconstructions, meniscus tears, ankle sprains, and chronic tendon issues.

Frequently Asked Questions

What equipment do I need for the off-season program? ▼

Access to a standard gym (barbells, dumbbells, trap bar, cables, resistance bands) is ideal. If you are training at home or with minimal equipment, we provide bodyweight and dumbbell regressions for every single drill.

How much time per week does the programme require? ▼

The 12-week season programme is structured into three clear phases designed to fit smoothly alongside your team trainings:

  • • Weeks 1 to 4 (Phase 1): 2 gym sessions and 1 mobility session per week.
  • • Weeks 5 to 8 (Phase 2): 2 gym sessions and 1 power session per week.
  • • Weeks 9 to 12 (Phase 3): 2 gym sessions and 2 field sessions per week.
What if I have an active hamstring, groin, or low back niggle right now? ▼

Phase 1 is specifically engineered for tissue tolerance and rehabilitation. You will learn isometric analgesic loading protocols that calm down irritated tendons while building eccentric strength. If you have an acute tear, nerve root symptoms, or post-surgical case, Tier 3 (1-on-1 Concierge) is recommended.

How does the video form review work in Tier 2? ▼

Simply record a 5–10 second clip of your lift (e.g. Nordic curl, split squat, plant cut) on your phone and email it to Justin. He replies with specific biomechanical cues and video feedback.
